what_it_is.prose: Saab is a Swedish defence and aerospace group with a deep Indian footprint in two pillars: (i) ground-combat weapons — Saab was awarded an Indian contract for AT4 anti-armour support weapons (announced March 2022) and is constructing India's first foreign-owned defence manufacturing facility, a Carl-Gustaf M4 factory in Haryana (construction began March 2024), making Saab the first OEM to leverage the new 74% FDI liberalisation; (ii) fighter aircraft — Saab is offering Gripen E for the Indian MRFA tender (114 fighters) and previously partnered with Adani (Sep 2017) before publicly stating in January 2023 that it would not partner Adani on Gripen local production. Saab continues to pitch Gripen for India with local production options as recently as February 2026.

faq.question: Is Saab building a Carl-Gustaf factory in India?
faq.answer: Yes. On 5 March 2024 Saab began construction of a new Carl-Gustaf manufacturing facility in Haryana, India — the first foreign-owned defence manufacturing facility in India under the post-2020 FDI liberalisation that allows up to 74% foreign ownership via government route.

faq.question: Did Saab partner with Adani to build Gripen in India?
faq.answer: Saab announced a collaboration plan with the Adani Group on 1 September 2017 to manufacture Gripen E fighters in India for the MRFA competition. However, in January 2023 Saab confirmed it would NOT partner Adani on Gripen local production, leaving Saab without a confirmed Indian industrial partner for the Gripen E MRFA offer.

faq.question: When did Saab get an Indian AT4 contract?
faq.answer: Saab was awarded an Indian contract for the AT4 anti-armour support weapon on 21 January 2022; deliveries have continued through 2025 alongside the Carl-Gustaf manufacturing facility construction.
